text:
maria: Heads up — we merged the kv-cache dependency bump that includes the CVE fix (cvE-2026-1234). Patch applied to staging at 12:17 UTC. Need post-update validation and canary plan.
liam: thx. I'll kick off a canary rollout to dedicated pool. plan: 5% traffic, run smoke + perf probes for 30m, watch p50/p95 and 5xx rates. rollback on >1% 5xx or p95 +50ms.
anya: +1 on thresholds. Also add audit events for KMS access during startup (we need the KMS key use logged). auditor-bot: audit: new key-use event logging enabled for service/redwood-runtime (rule id: AUD-2026-07).
liam: starting canary now — deploy-bot, please run canary to gv-kvcache-srv:v2.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: service=gv-kvcache-srv image=gv-kvcache-srv:v2 traffic=5% region=us-west-2 canary_id=canary-1789998765
liam: smoke tests: 
```
# smoke test script run by eng-sre
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.io/gv/cache/validate -d '{"key":"smoke-1"}' | jq .status
# expect: {"status":"ok","latency_ms":<20>}
```
liam: smoke logs (first 10 lines):
```
[00:12:21] validate: ok latency=12ms
[00:12:22] validate: ok latency=14ms
[00:12:23] validate: ok latency=11ms
```
maria: good. please also run a parity test against previous kv-cache version for correctness (100 random keys).
liam: running parity now — small script, 100 keys, look for mismatches.
liam: parity result: 100/100 matches. no data corruption.
sophie: watching prod-like traces — I see a tiny p95 bump in us-west-2 at minute 18 (+12ms), overall throughput same. errors: 0.12% 5xx in that region during canary window.
maria: 0.12% is above our desired 0.05% but below rollback threshold. think we should keep observing for 30m. check logs for stacktraces.
liam: pulled recent logs: one stacktrace pattern pointing at kvcache::serialize when handling long keys (>1024 chars). only 3 traces.
anya: are long keys common? we have a fallback path that should truncate — can we validate truncation logic?
sophie: those requests look synthetic from integration tests hitting long keys. production traffic doesn't hit that path often.
maria: ok mark as low severity for now, but add a follow-up ticket to harden serialize path. assign to eng-runtime.
liam: canary at 5% completed 30m. metrics summary: p50 +2ms, p95 +12ms (us-west-2), global 5xx delta +0.03%. no crash loops. canary status: healthy per thresholds.
deploy-bot: Canary canary-1789998765 promoted to 100% (rolling). rollout start=1789998769 end=1789999000 strategy=rolling max_unavailable=1
maria: before we close, please capture KMS audit entries and S3 access patterns during rollout and attach to the ticket. auditor-bot: audit: recorded rollout event canary-1789998765 by liam; k8s:deployment/gv-kvcache-srv image=gv-kvcache-srv:v2.
liam: uploaded perf dashboards + dumped flamegraphs to /artifacts/canary-1789998765. short-term action: create runtime PR to guard against long-key serialization and add unit tests.
anya: release note: dependency kv-cache@2.3.1 (security fix CVE-2026-1234) rolled out to prod. mark release as security-patch and notify customers in next weekly digest.
maria: assigning ticket SEC-4567: "kv-cache long-key serialize hardening" to @eng-runtime. severity: P3 (post-deploy observation).
sophie: will keep an eye on p95 and 5xx for next 24h, pinging if it creeps. :eyes:
liam: closing thread — thanks everyone, filing retro notes for the canary.
maria: thanks. good to have audit trail and parity checks included. :thumbsup:
